```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


Reading in data as homicides R object 

```{r}

library(readr)
library(tidyverse)

homicides <- read_csv("~/R_Programming_for_Research_ERHS_535/Homework 5 - Reproducible research #2/data/homicide-data.csv")

homicides <- homicides %>%
  mutate(city_name = paste(city, state, sep = ", "))

```


Filtering to one city (Atlanta) and removing missing coordinates 

```{r}

atl_homicides <- homicides %>% 
  filter(city_name == "Atlanta, GA") %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon))

```


Adding a solved vs unsolved column (status) in the data frame

```{r}

# ?case_when

atl_solved <- atl_homicides %>%
  mutate(status = case_when(
    disposition == "Closed by arrest" ~ "Solved",
    disposition %in% c("Closed without arrest","Open/No arrest") ~ "Unsolved"))

```

Creating a new column for top 3 race groups with the highest number of homicides in Atlanta

```{r}

library(forcats)

# ?fct_lump

atl_top3 <- atl_solved %>%
  mutate(race_top3 = fct_lump(victim_race, n = 3,
                              other_level = "Other"))

```

Converting latitude and longitude columns into sf objects

```{r}

library(sf)

# ?st_as_sf

atl_sf <- st_as_sf(atl_top3, coords = c("lon", "lat"),
                   crs = 4326)


```
